newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris may tender five more Caspian oilfields.
newsitem.headline: Azeris may tender five more Caspian oilfields.

text.p: Azerbaijan will probably hold tenders for five more oilfields in the Caspian Sea as part of its drive to lure foreign energy investors to one of the world's newest energy regions.
Vitaly Belyarbekov, deputy head of foreign investment at Azeri state oil company SOCAR, told an international energy conference in Baku that the tenders would probably be held from early next year.
"A possible tender in all likelihood will occur in the first quarter of 1998," he said.
He said the sites on offer would include the legendary but ageing Neftanniye Kamni (Oil Rocks) -- the world's first major offshore drilling platform.
Also included were the Palchyg Talesi, Bakhar and Bulla-More fields, and a group of four reserves -- Sangachaly-Morye, Dubannyi-Morye, Khara and Zira.
SOCAR estimates total recoverable reserves at all the five fields at least 100 million tonnes.
Belyarbekov said parts of the fields were in deep water and had not been explored.

Oil Rocks, the most productive of the five sites, is a Soviet-era "city on the water" of ageing rigs connected by a maze of dilapidated wooden and concrete platforms. It produces about 700,000 tonnes of crude yearly (14,000 bpd) -- a drop in the ocean compared to its former glory days.
Belyarbekov said each field needed rehabilitation and feasibility studies being carried out by SOCAR and MAI Consultants Ltd and which would be completed next year.
Azerbaijan already has five major deals worth over $18 billion with foreign oil and gas companies which will develop reserves in the Azeri sector of the Caspian.

The largest contract -- with the Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC) consortium led by British Petroleum and Statoil (Den norske stats oljeselskap) -- is due to start producing early oil from its $8 billion project in August.
SOCAR President Natik Aliyev said on Wednesday that four more contracts with foreign firms to develop new fields would be signed by the end of this year.
Many existing SOCAR fields are in a state of disrepair and need foreign help and technology to function.
